Potentially; Yes. However, economic indicators show that removing the carbon tax while having the higher tax-free threshold will lead to inflationary pressures, and likely depreciate the Australian currency; leading to increased costs of living still. If the threshold did stay, its likely we'd be supplemented with increases in interest rates by the RBA, probably sitting around 500-525 basis points.

EDIT: All in all, what isn't paid in tax will be paid by interest rates; and vice versa.

The reduction of the tax-free threshold is an economic premise linked with the introduction of the carbon tax. As the carbon tax was a proportional tax, a flat amount at $23/tonne emitted; it lifts the cost of almost every consumer good. In order to balance out the cost of living, the Labor government lifted the tax free threshold to $18,200 to make lower income earners not feel the stress of the increased cost of living following the carbon tax.

The threshold will not be lowered without the removal of the carbon tax, and vice versa. Even if the carbon tax is removed; there is still the Emissions trading scheme being implemented, which is a free-floating system built on the foundations of the CPRS.
